proposal.title: Replace the Aurelia launch presentation with the revised main-stage programme
proposal.reason: Replace only the Aurelia launch marketing presentation in campaign.ncc1978 with the author’s revised sequence. Preserve the steering-wheel analogy, everyday-use commercials, live demonstration, partner panel and four follow-up dates. Put key values and canonical references in parameters. The author explicitly requests the pricing discussion and free rebroadcast/certification terms; no prices, unprovided durations or unnamed representative identities are invented. Keep the launch event reference, campaign ownership and all other marketing steps unchanged.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
before.objective: Introduce Aurelia and its business software through press and television advertising, NCC presentations, a ComputerLand sales premiere and the public launch of Logix Computer Academy.
message: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia through newspaper and business-press teasers, then invite customers and press to the premiere.

marketing_presentation.description: Begin newspaper and business-press teasers on {start_date}, introducing Aurelia as a personal assistant in business. Start with “coming this spring”, then publish the {premiere_date} premiere date and invite brochure and presentation-invitation requests.

Follow the teasers with explanatory print advertisements about Aurelia, Abacus and independently branded BPI applications. Prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage, so readers can act on the campaign through local demonstrations and training enquiries.

During late May and early June, organise joint Logix/BPI press previews, prepare dealers and demonstration staff, issue launch invitations and rehearse the Aurelia presentation. Staff telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demonstration appointments and Academy bookings.

marketing_steps.description: Run the cinematic Aurelia television commercial and direct viewers to demonstrations.

marketing_presentation.description: The proposed advertisement is a {duration_seconds}-second film trailer, with {lead} proposed as its lead. In the final {reveal_seconds} seconds, show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, the logo and the June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable, independently branded BPI report; explain accounting in the accompanying press campaign and follow-up films. Casting remains subject to contract.

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration. Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence. Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia as a business assistant at NCC on 5 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter} introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with {presenter}’s investment, AION/Logix cooperation and AION’s C/TUI redevelopment commitments disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice and direct ordering. Announce the official Academy launch on June 16, including BPI-authorised training, direct distribution and the dealer programme. Present confirmed course locations and schedules; specialist support is provided by BPI.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. State complete package contents, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the June 6 morning developer presentation and afternoon BPI session, the June 14 ComputerLand sales premiere and the June 16 Academy launch. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training and setup arrangements.
Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.
Moderated questions follow the presentation.
Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

Rehearse the digital-video projection and recording path, display readability, lighting and sound in the hired room. Have a backup demonstration system and an explicitly identified recorded fallback available.

marketing_steps.description: Present AION C IDE and the Software Developer Package on the morning of 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Introduce the platform interfaces that the Software Developer Package exposes: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation and licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development. Explain how those interfaces support application and peripheral work on Aurelia.

Use {ide} with {sdk} to edit a small application with syntax highlighting and diagnostic navigation. Build it using a qualified optimization profile, link an assembly library and debug the application in RAM. Explain C source portability and the need for separate target builds rather than promising universal binary compatibility.

Demonstrate keyboard-operated TUI forms with bounded data controls and calls into the shared ROM TUI. Show text and bitmap presentation in tested modes, distinguishing SDK composite helpers from native ROM services. Publish measured memory, disk and performance results; shared source and API contracts do not imply that future targets have already been released.

marketing_steps.description: Present the independent BPI business applications on the afternoon of 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in this dedicated session.
{provider} covers setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage.

Use pilot demonstrations with {pilot_businesses} businesses and several accounting practices to prepare representative BPI workflows. Reconcile their results against existing records, checking data volumes, disk and RAM requirements, posting, corrections, backup and restore, payroll jurisdiction coverage and the summary export to Abacus. Publish measured capacity and supported configurations without treating pilot targets as completed results.

marketing_steps.description: Hold the official Aurelia sales premiere at a ComputerLand shop on 14 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: {dealer} hosts the official Aurelia sales premiere with {logix}. Introduce the retail offering, demonstrate the business-assistant workflow and help visitors choose a suitable system and associated software. Keep separately licensed BPI applications and training distinct from the computer purchase.

marketing_steps.description: Officially launch Logix Computer Academy and its BPI programme on 16 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: The Academy was established on {established_date} and is announced publicly on {announcement_date}. Officially launch on {launch_date} with an initial {city_count}-city US programme with a {fundamentals_days}-day Fundamentals course. Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases. Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.

The {launch_date} Academy launch includes BPI-authorised practical courses and direct distribution, dealer qualification, accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist. Dealers handle first-line installation enquiries, BPI handles software defects and specialist support, and Logix supports hardware. Training, setup services and software licences remain separate offerings. Train instructors and dealers to explain advertised modules, published requirements and support boundaries.

marketing_steps.description: Record the NCC presentations and distribute cleared television coverage.

marketing_presentation.description: Before NCC, contact television stations and arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights for redistribution. Include Michael Douglas commercial footage only if it is separately cleared for that use.

Throughout 5–8 June 1978, use a professional multi-camera crew to record every Logix NCC presentation and hands-on demonstration, including the premiere, technical and developer content, partner appearances, additional sessions and questions. Capture clean presenter audio, audience reactions and close-ups of the computer, display, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

Preserve demonstration fidelity: do not accelerate startup or recalculation, hide failures with misleading cuts or present recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and any recorded fallback.

After NCC, prepare a business-user broadcast feature, short station-ready news and demonstration excerpts, clean captioned footage, separate narration or audio where practical, a factual product and Academy press sheet, and full edited presentations for longer technical coverage. Offer cleared, Logix-identified material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication, dispatch and station-compatible copies. Distribution follows editing and clearance. Stations choose their own participation, schedules and editorial selection; no airtime or endorsement is guaranteed.

marketing_steps.description: Plan year-end workshops and customer-led expansion after the launch.

marketing_presentation.description: Prepare year-end workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations, specifying payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Keep customer data under customer control and obtain consent before presenting referrals as accountant endorsements. This is follow-up planning, not a claim that year-end work is complete within the campaign period.

Plan expansion of demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results, explaining the module-to-suite upgrade route. BPI support for the Model II remains a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia as a business assistant at NCC on 5 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Present on the {stage}, using {projector_count} video projectors. Record the full presentation and make it available to television broadcasters under {rebroadcast_terms}.
Open with the {computer} television commercial.

{presenter} describes {development_period} of work to bring {computer} to market. Early cars used tillers, levers, rotary cranks and cross-shaped handles before the steering wheel became the familiar standard. Personal computers reached an important milestone in {assembled_computer_year}: buyers no longer had to assemble them. Yet their controls still resemble those early experiments—awkward, inconsistent and hard to learn. He introduces Aurelia as a computer with a steering wheel: a consistent, intuitive way to work.

{presenter} reveals {computer_count} Aurelia computers. A camera circles them, showing every angle on the projection screens. Then show {commercial_count} new commercials: a housewife prints recipes, a schoolboy uses the on-screen calculator, and a businessman checks his diary of meetings and tasks.

{presenter} switches on {computer} and opens the {tools} menu. He loads a text document from disk, demonstrates editing, cursor navigation and selection, and copies and pastes text. He then finds a contact in the directory and pastes its details into the document, showing how familiar actions carry across applications.
{presenter} connects a printer while the computer remains on and prints the document. He demonstrates the calculator and a calendar of tasks and events, then prints the next day’s schedule.

{presenter} connects another disk drive and loads {spreadsheet} from disk. He explains its rules and calculations, then opens a large, complex accounting sheet. Changing one input immediately updates calculations throughout the sheet; he prints the result. He asks, “How many commands did I have to memorise?” to underline that the audience has followed familiar actions rather than memorised instructions.

{presenter} invites {os_speaker} from {os_company}, {logix_speaker} from {computer_company}, {software_speaker} from {software_company}, and a representative of {retailer} onto the stage. He introduces the {platform_bits}-bit platform, with its specifications displayed on the screens.

{speaker} explains that Aurelia runs applications for {compatible_version} and introduces {new_version} with a text user interface. The operating system belongs to {owner} and is available to other manufacturers whose hardware meets its requirements. He thanks {partner} for supporting this approach.
{speaker} presents Aurelia pricing and the {support_levels}-level support system, including telephone help through a call centre.

{speaker} introduces the {ide} and announces its presentation on {developer_session}. He explains that {software_company} and {application_company} have ported their applications to C and the new user interface; the business applications will be demonstrated on {business_session}.
The {retailer} representative announces product availability in its shops from {retail_date}. {speaker} introduces {academy}, opening on {academy_date}, and the try-before-you-buy programme.

{presenter} explains {company}’s plans for expansion cards, FlexiBUS devices and monitors: limited further in-house development, with third-party products welcomed. Products meeting the compatibility criteria can receive {certification} under {certification_terms}. He invites everyone to try Aurelia at the booth.

Close with questions and answers. Keep reminders on screen for the C development session ({developer_session}), BPI presentation ({business_session}), ComputerLand sales premiere ({retail_date}) and Logix Academy launch ({academy_date}).

audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia through newspaper and business-press teasers, then invite customers and press to the premiere.

marketing_presentation.description: Begin newspaper and business-press teasers on {start_date}, introducing Aurelia as a personal assistant in business. Start with “coming this spring”, then publish the {premiere_date} premiere date and invite brochure and presentation-invitation requests.

Follow the teasers with explanatory print advertisements about Aurelia, Abacus and independently branded BPI applications. Prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage, so readers can act on the campaign through local demonstrations and training enquiries.

During late May and early June, organise joint Logix/BPI press previews, prepare dealers and demonstration staff, issue launch invitations and rehearse the Aurelia presentation. Staff telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demonstration appointments and Academy bookings.

marketing_steps.description: Run the cinematic Aurelia television commercial and direct viewers to demonstrations.

marketing_presentation.description: The proposed advertisement is a {duration_seconds}-second film trailer, with {lead} proposed as its lead. In the final {reveal_seconds} seconds, show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, the logo and the June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable, independently branded BPI report; explain accounting in the accompanying press campaign and follow-up films. Casting remains subject to contract.

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration. Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence. Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia as a business assistant at NCC on 5 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Present on the {stage}, using {projector_count} video projectors. Record the full presentation and make it available to television broadcasters under {rebroadcast_terms}.
Open with the {computer} television commercial.

{presenter} describes {development_period} of work to bring {computer} to market. Early cars used tillers, levers, rotary cranks and cross-shaped handles before the steering wheel became the familiar standard. Personal computers reached an important milestone in {assembled_computer_year}: buyers no longer had to assemble them. Yet their controls still resemble those early experiments—awkward, inconsistent and hard to learn. He introduces Aurelia as a computer with a steering wheel: a consistent, intuitive way to work.

{presenter} reveals {computer_count} Aurelia computers. A camera circles them, showing every angle on the projection screens. Then show {commercial_count} new commercials: a housewife prints recipes, a schoolboy uses the on-screen calculator, and a businessman checks his diary of meetings and tasks.

{presenter} switches on {computer} and opens the {tools} menu. He loads a text document from disk, demonstrates editing, cursor navigation and selection, and copies and pastes text. He then finds a contact in the directory and pastes its details into the document, showing how familiar actions carry across applications.
{presenter} connects a printer while the computer remains on and prints the document. He demonstrates the calculator and a calendar of tasks and events, then prints the next day’s schedule.

{presenter} connects another disk drive and loads {spreadsheet} from disk. He explains its rules and calculations, then opens a large, complex accounting sheet. Changing one input immediately updates calculations throughout the sheet; he prints the result. He asks, “How many commands did I have to memorise?” to underline that the audience has followed familiar actions rather than memorised instructions.

{presenter} invites {os_speaker} from {os_company}, {logix_speaker} from {computer_company}, {software_speaker} from {software_company}, and a representative of {retailer} onto the stage. He introduces the {platform_bits}-bit platform, with its specifications displayed on the screens.

{speaker} explains that Aurelia runs applications for {compatible_version} and introduces {new_version} with a text user interface. The operating system belongs to {owner} and is available to other manufacturers whose hardware meets its requirements. He thanks {partner} for supporting this approach.
{speaker} presents Aurelia pricing and the {support_levels}-level support system, including telephone help through a call centre.

{speaker} introduces the {ide} and announces its presentation on {developer_session}. He explains that {software_company} and {application_company} have ported their applications to C and the new user interface; the business applications will be demonstrated on {business_session}.
The {retailer} representative announces product availability in its shops from {retail_date}. {speaker} introduces {academy}, opening on {academy_date}, and the try-before-you-buy programme.

{presenter} explains {company}’s plans for expansion cards, FlexiBUS devices and monitors: limited further in-house development, with third-party products welcomed. Products meeting the compatibility criteria can receive {certification} under {certification_terms}. He invites everyone to try Aurelia at the booth.

Close with questions and answers. Keep reminders on screen for the C development session ({developer_session}), BPI presentation ({business_session}), ComputerLand sales premiere ({retail_date}) and Logix Academy launch ({academy_date}).

marketing_steps.description: Present AION C IDE and the Software Developer Package on the morning of 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Introduce the platform interfaces that the Software Developer Package exposes: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation and licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development. Explain how those interfaces support application and peripheral work on Aurelia.

Use {ide} with {sdk} to edit a small application with syntax highlighting and diagnostic navigation. Build it using a qualified optimization profile, link an assembly library and debug the application in RAM. Explain C source portability and the need for separate target builds rather than promising universal binary compatibility.

Demonstrate keyboard-operated TUI forms with bounded data controls and calls into the shared ROM TUI. Show text and bitmap presentation in tested modes, distinguishing SDK composite helpers from native ROM services. Publish measured memory, disk and performance results; shared source and API contracts do not imply that future targets have already been released.

marketing_steps.description: Present the independent BPI business applications on the afternoon of 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in this dedicated session.
{provider} covers setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage.

Use pilot demonstrations with {pilot_businesses} businesses and several accounting practices to prepare representative BPI workflows. Reconcile their results against existing records, checking data volumes, disk and RAM requirements, posting, corrections, backup and restore, payroll jurisdiction coverage and the summary export to Abacus. Publish measured capacity and supported configurations without treating pilot targets as completed results.

marketing_steps.description: Hold the official Aurelia sales premiere at a ComputerLand shop on 14 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: {dealer} hosts the official Aurelia sales premiere with {logix}. Introduce the retail offering, demonstrate the business-assistant workflow and help visitors choose a suitable system and associated software. Keep separately licensed BPI applications and training distinct from the computer purchase.

marketing_steps.description: Officially launch Logix Computer Academy and its BPI programme on 16 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: The Academy was established on {established_date} and is announced publicly on {announcement_date}. Officially launch on {launch_date} with an initial {city_count}-city US programme with a {fundamentals_days}-day Fundamentals course. Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases. Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.

The {launch_date} Academy launch includes BPI-authorised practical courses and direct distribution, dealer qualification, accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist. Dealers handle first-line installation enquiries, BPI handles software defects and specialist support, and Logix supports hardware. Training, setup services and software licences remain separate offerings. Train instructors and dealers to explain advertised modules, published requirements and support boundaries.

marketing_steps.description: Record the NCC presentations and distribute cleared television coverage.

marketing_presentation.description: Before NCC, contact television stations and arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights for redistribution. Include Michael Douglas commercial footage only if it is separately cleared for that use.

Throughout 5–8 June 1978, use a professional multi-camera crew to record every Logix NCC presentation and hands-on demonstration, including the premiere, technical and developer content, partner appearances, additional sessions and questions. Capture clean presenter audio, audience reactions and close-ups of the computer, display, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.

Preserve demonstration fidelity: do not accelerate startup or recalculation, hide failures with misleading cuts or present recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and any recorded fallback.

After NCC, prepare a business-user broadcast feature, short station-ready news and demonstration excerpts, clean captioned footage, separate narration or audio where practical, a factual product and Academy press sheet, and full edited presentations for longer technical coverage. Offer cleared, Logix-identified material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication, dispatch and station-compatible copies. Distribution follows editing and clearance. Stations choose their own participation, schedules and editorial selection; no airtime or endorsement is guaranteed.

marketing_steps.description: Plan year-end workshops and customer-led expansion after the launch.

marketing_presentation.description: Prepare year-end workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations, specifying payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Keep customer data under customer control and obtain consent before presenting referrals as accountant endorsements. This is follow-up planning, not a claim that year-end work is complete within the campaign period.

Plan expansion of demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results, explaining the module-to-suite upgrade route. BPI support for the Model II remains a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.
